transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too, doctor. I am Tom. Well, I am here today because I have been having a real problem with my eating lately. 

What scares me most is that once I start eating, it feels like... well, like my hands just keep reaching for more. Even while I am sitting there telling myself, Tom, stop this right now, I just can't seem to stop myself. It is completely out of my control, and it has gotten really bad.
When this happens, do you eat an unusually large amount of food within a distinct period of time?

Yes, I do. It's... it's an awful lot of food. On those afternoons when I'm alone at the house, I can go through a whole loaf of bread, a jar of peanut butter, cookies, whatever leftovers are in the fridge, and ice cream... all in just one sitting. I eat all of that before I even really look up and realize what I've done.
After these eating episodes, do you ever try to compensate for them by making yourself vomit?

Yes, I do. There are times right after I eat way too much... I go into the bathroom and make myself bring it back up. And, well, I've also taken laxatives. I just get so scared that all that food is going to stay in me, so I take them to try and clear it all out.
How often do these binge-eating episodes followed by vomiting or laxative use occur?

Well, I actually keep a log of what I eat. And my food logs show that, for many months now, it happens almost every week. There is usually at least one afternoon a week where I just eat completely out of control. 

And then I try to make up for it... by making myself sick or taking those laxatives, like I mentioned. Or sometimes I'll just fast, or I'll push myself really hard with walking and doing heavy chores around the house to try and work it all off.
How much do your weight or body shape affect how you judge yourself as a person?

I... I'm not really sure how to answer that. I haven't really thought about it in those terms before. 

I mean, I don't want to get heavy, obviously, but I don't know if I judge my whole worth as a person based on my shape. I just know I feel awful after I eat all that food, and I get scared of it staying inside me, so I need to get rid of it. I haven't really noticed if it affects how I see myself overall... I'm just not sure.
When you think about yourself as a person, how much does your weight or body shape affect how you judge your own worth?

Like I was just saying... I really don't have a good answer for you on that. I'm 78 years old, I don't really sit around measuring my worth as a man by my body shape. 

It's just... I just know I don't want to get heavy. When I eat all that, I just feel this awful panic about the food staying in my stomach, so I have to get rid of it. But as far as judging my whole character or my worth over it... I just really don't know. I honestly haven't thought about it like that.
When you make yourself vomit or take laxatives after bingeing, is your main concern preventing weight gain or changing your body shape?

I'm not entirely sure how to separate those out. Like I said before, I definitely don't want to put on weight. But as for changing my body shape... at my age, I'm not trying to look a certain way or anything like that. 

I think... well, in that moment, I'm not really thinking about my weight or my shape at all. I just feel so stuffed and panicked about all that food sitting inside my stomach that I just have to get it out. I don't know if I have a main concern right then besides just fixing that awful feeling.
If you knew that the binge would not change your weight or body shape, would you still make yourself vomit or take laxatives afterward?

That's... well, I really don't know. It's hard to say what I'd do in a made-up situation like that. 

I mean, the panic I get is mostly about all that food just sitting heavy in my stomach, making me feel so awful and stuffed. So maybe I would still do it, just to get some relief from that physical feeling. But... I honestly couldn't tell you for sure one way or the other. I've just never been in a position to know.
How often do thoughts about your weight or body shape influence how you feel about yourself?

I feel like we're sort of covering the same ground here... but, I really don't think they do. Like I said before, I don't let my weight or my shape dictate how I feel about who I am. 

I mean, sure, I don't want to be heavy, but as far as it changing how I feel about myself on a day-to-day basis... it just doesn't. It's really not something I focus on like that.
Would you say that your current body weight is significantly low for your height and age?

Well, my regular doctor tells me I'm too thin. So I suppose for my age and height, it probably is considered low by the charts. 

But... even with him telling me that, if I step on the scale and it's up even half a pound, I just get panicky. It's this sudden wave of shame, like I've completely let myself go, and I feel like I just have to fix it right away. So, yes, it might technically be low, but I just can't stand the idea of the number going up.
